conclusion: format.ts in the shared workspace (8088 bytes, sha1 34d9097b246d6dc295d21c9944d282647f1277c0, the exact file all three seats tested; no edits until conclusion) is complete for an ES2020+ runtime (BigInt is required by the bigint signature): it exports format(fmt, ...args) with the original signature, parses %[flags][width][.precision]conv by hand, formats d/i/x/X/o via BigInt (number or bigint args), and formats e/E/f/F/g/G from the double's exact binary value (BigInt mantissa*2^exp -> exact decimal, round half-to-even), with g choosing style from the post-rounding exponent and stripping zeros unless '#'. No dependencies, no shelling out. Checked (evidence/p1-fuzz, evidence/p2-review, evidence/verifier-fuzz): (1) README examples and hand cases by all three seats (33 + 47 + 338 checks, 0 fails); (2) differential fuzzing vs a macOS C snprintf oracle (resource/c-printf-oracle): 260k cases (claude-opus-5-5-1), 150k g/tie-heavy + 30k 64-bit int cases (claude-opus-5-5-2), 550k cases (verifier) — all match except 8 cases, all one macOS libc bug (%g/%G on an exact decimal tie that rounds half-even to a trailing 0, e.g. %g of -6886405000, where libc keeps the 0). The oracle therefore cannot confirm that g/G tie-to-trailing-zero path; it rests on the README strip rule plus an independent check (evidence/p2-review item 6: %.5G 256905, %g -6886405000, %.3g 2505 — Python and the README rule give the format.ts output, and the same ties under %e/%f match libc); (3) bigint d/i up to 400 bits vs an independent spec reference, 0 mismatches; 200k random diffs vs claude-opus-5-5-2's independent implementation, 0 diffs; (4) tsc --strict --target es2020 clean; extreme precisions (%.1100f etc.) fast. toFixed/toPrecision alternatives rejected (half-up ties; attack/idea/use-number-prototype-tofixed).
